subject.title: [Bug]: macOS Chat window causes excessive GPU pressure when in foreground (Metal rendering overhead on Apple Silicon)

question: Which native macOS Chat performance target should guide remediation: preserve per-token immediacy, coalesce streaming/scroll updates within a bounded latency budget, or prioritize a broader native-chat rendering redesign?
rationale: The report establishes a performance concern but not the responsible rendering work or acceptable latency/UX tradeoff, so code inspection alone cannot safely choose the product behavior.

options.title: Profile then coalesce updates
options.body: Define a bounded streaming-latency budget and pursue narrowly measured update and auto-scroll coalescing after a representative Apple Silicon trace.

options.title: Preserve current streaming cadence
options.body: Treat the observed foreground rendering cost as acceptable unless profiling shows a regression beyond an agreed power or responsiveness threshold.

options.title: Fold into macOS redesign
options.body: Defer performance changes to the broader native macOS chat redesign if maintainers want one coordinated rendering architecture decision.

recommendation.title: Profile then coalesce updates
recommendation.body: Define a bounded streaming-latency budget and pursue narrowly measured update and auto-scroll coalescing after a representative Apple Silicon trace.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available adjacent native-chat routing candidate in the provided merged and active-work history.
